ACME Ops: Hey team — saw a big charge spike for acct acme-corp. Dashboard shows ~120k tokens for 2025-11-11 but invoice line shows ~240k. Can we check if retries caused double metering?
Alex S.: Sorry you're seeing that. Can you paste the example request_id(s) or timestamp range?
ACME Ops: Sure — sample request ids: req_0a1b2c3, req_0a1b2c4, around 2025-11-11T18:12:xxZ. Client reported timeout then retried.
Maria (Billing): Linking to ledger entries now. If retries replayed through gateway without idempotency the ledger might record duplicate tokens. I need a request_id -> event_id mapping.
ACME Ops: Here's the relevant log lines (sanitized):
```
2025-11-11T18:12:08Z request=req_0a1b2c3 status=timeout client_retry=true
2025-11-11T18:12:09Z request=req_0a1b2c3 status=completed tokens=412
2025-11-11T18:12:12Z request=req_0a1b2c4 status=completed tokens=415
```
Alex S.: Hmm looks like client retried with a new request id (req_0a1b2c4) and gateway accepted both. ingress-bot, can you dump ingest path traces for those req_ids?
ingress-bot: Traces attached: route=gw-v2 -> frontend -> billing-ingest -> ledger. Both requests reached billing-ingest within 4s of each other. idempotency-key header missing.
Jon R.: If idempotency-key wasn't provided then our ingress treats each as distinct and we meter both. We normally deduplicate when same idempotency-key or same request_id is replayed, but only for identical request_id AND same client-id.
Priya Eng: Two failure modes: client generates new request id on retry (so no dedupe) OR gateway retries the same request but strips idempotency. Here client retried with a new id so gateway had no way to dedupe.
Maria (Billing): That would explain ~2x tokens for those flows. Can we quantify how many requests look like this in the 11/11 18:00-19:00 window?
Alex S.: Running quick query against ingestion:
```
SELECT count(*) FROM meter_events
WHERE account='acme-corp' AND time >= '2025-11-11T18:00:00Z' AND time < '2025-11-11T19:00:00Z'
AND (client_retry = true OR request_replayed = true);
```
Result: 1,872 events flagged as client_retry in that window. Average token per event ~410 -> approx 767k tokens attributed to retries.
ACME Ops: Ugh. Their client retry policy is naive: retries on any timeout, generates new id each time.
Jon R.: For immediate remediation we can a) issue a billing credit for duplicate meter events that match our dedupe heuristic, and b) add a short-term guard in billing-ingest to collapse near-duplicate requests for same account+prompt hash arriving within 10s.
Maria (Billing): I support a credit. I'll open a refund ticket once engineering provides the dedupe list. Please produce a CSV of suspect event_ids and token counts.
Priya Eng: I'll generate the list. Heuristic: same account, prompt hash equal, client IP same, timestamps within 30s, different request_ids. We'll tag events with reason=retry-replay.
Alex S.: Also note: dashboard token counts use streaming-aggregator which dedupes by idempotency-key when present, but invoice pipeline uses raw ledger totals today. So dashboards may undercount or overcount depending on where dedupe happened. We should document this discrepancy to customers.
ACME Ops: Appreciate that. Timeline on credit?
Maria (Billing): I'll queue the credit after we get the CSV. Expect 2-3 business days for processing and reflected on next statement or as a one-off credit.
Jon R.: Longer-term fixes: 1) educate SDKs to set Idempotency-Key by default, 2) add server-side best-effort replay detection based on prompt-hash+client, 3) surface a "duplicate-suspect" flag in the console to let customers opt into auto-crediting.
ACME Ops: SDK changes help. Can you share recommended retry logic?
Alex S.: Minimal: exponential backoff, preserve idempotency-key across retries, treat HTTP 408/499 as retryable only once. Example header: `Idempotency-Key: <uuid-v4>` on initial attempt, reuse for retries.
ACME Ops: We'll patch SDK and roll to prod tomorrow. Please send the CSV when ready.
Priya Eng: CSV uploaded to internal bucket s3://redwood-support/acme/retry-dedupe-1835001234.csv. Contains 1872 rows with event_id, request_id, tokens, prompt_hash, client_ip, ts, reason.
Maria (Billing): Received. Processing credit now. Posting refund ticket #BILL-8721.
Alex S.: I'll follow up in 24h with monitoring for any residual replay spikes. Ping me if you see anything else. :thumbsup:
ACME Ops: Thanks — looking forward to the credit and the SDK guidance.
Maria (Billing): Credit applied, will show as adjustment on next invoice. Closing once confirmed by ACME.
ACME Ops: Confirmed refund on 2025-11-15, amount matches expectation. Thanks everyone.
